subject: SummitCare SDK auth + model-policy handoff

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: SummitCare SDK auth + model-policy handoff

Hi Emma / SummitCare team,

Thanks again for the call today — great to hear more about your clinician triage workflow and the strict PII controls you need. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side so we can get an engineering handoff scheduled: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Private deployment preferred (VPC connector) for PHI routing and audit controls.
- SAML/Okta/Azure AD single sign-on for your admin console.
- SDK integration points: server-side calls for generation, client-side for embeddings only.
- Model routing: low-latency path for triage (sub-150ms target), lower-cost fallback for batch line-item processing.
- Embeddings + reranker: embeddings at 1536 dim (open-model), reranker inference must return in <= 200ms for a 5-10 candidate set.

Attachments I’m sending with this message: MVP-integration-checklist.xlsx and SummitCare_Security_Questions.pdf — the checklist maps our SDK endpoints to your integration touchpoints; the security doc covers SOC2 scoping and what we can provide.

Proposed technical next steps:
1) You share a technical point-of-contact (name + availability) for a 30–45m handoff call next week.
2) We deliver a draft routing/policy config (latency/cost thresholds, fallback chain) and a short SDK auth snippet (API key, mTLS, or OIDC options) for you to review.
3) If private deployment is required, we’ll exchange network requirements and SAML metadata; I’ve asked our infra lead (cc’ed) to prepare a draft.

Can you confirm the tech contact and preferred time windows? Once confirmed we’ll send the routing-policy-draft.yaml and a short walkthrough.

Best,
Ben Carter

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 20:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitCare SDK auth + model-policy handoff

Ben — copying a brief draft of the routing/policy we discussed. I’ve kept this high level so it’s easy to iterate with SummitCare’s tech lead: 

--- routing-policy-draft.yaml (inline snippet) ---
# primary: low-latency route (dedicated pool in us-west)
primary:
  model: rwd-llama-13b-llm-lowlat
  latency_slo_ms: 150
  batch_size: auto
  cache: prefix_kv_enabled
  region: us-west-2

# fallback chain: cost-aware then cross-region
fallbacks:
  - model: rwd-llama-13b-quantized
    condition: tokens_per_minute > 12000 OR avg_latency > 200
  - model: rwd-llama-7b-hosted
    condition: primary_unavailable
    region: us-east-1

# reranker config
reranker:
  endpoint: /v1/rr/rerank
  timeout_ms: 200
  top_k: 10
--- end snippet ---

Notes:
- Latency SLOs are for tail p95; we should confirm whether SummitCare measures on-server or end-to-end (SDK->client).
- For auth, we prefer short-lived OIDC tokens for admin console and mTLS for private node-to-node traffic. We can provide a sample OIDC client config if they want Okta/Azure AD.

I’ll attach the full routing-policy-draft.yaml in the next message to the customer. If Karthik has infra notes (network ports, peering) add them and I’ll include on the handoff call.

—Lauren
Product Solutions Engineer
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and aligns with what we need. A few clarifying Qs from our engineering side before the call: 

1) Embeddings dimension: we’re building multi-modal search; can you confirm the default embedding vector size for your recommended model and whether we can downsample?
2) Reranker latency: your 200ms timeout — is that server-only or measured end-to-end? We’d prefer an end-to-end SLA for the interactive triage UI.
3) Auth: we use Azure AD; can you supply SAML and OIDC examples? For private deployment we’ll need the SAML metadata and network egress rules.

Tech lead Ryan is available Tue/Wed next week (Apr 6–7) in the US-PDT morning window. Please put Lauren/Karthik on the invite so we can walk through the routing file.

Great — thanks Emma. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Embeddings: our recommended embedding model returns 1536-d vectors by default for that family. We can provide a lightweight 512-d projection in the SDK if you want to trade quality for storage/cost.

2) Reranker latency: the 200ms timeout in the routing snippet is server-side. For the triage UI we typically recommend targeting 250–300ms end-to-end accounting for network and client processing. If you need a hard 200ms E2E SLO we’ll map the budget (server 120ms, network 40ms, client 40ms) and adjust routing to favor lower-token models and increased batching.

3) Auth: we’ll attach SAML metadata and an OIDC client example in the infra packet. For private deployment we require a CIDR range and a list of outbound ports — Karthik, can you attach the network checklist?

Next steps (agreed):
- I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue Apr 6 09:30 PDT — 45m handoff (Lauren + Karthik + Ryan).
- We’ll attach the full routing-policy-draft.yaml and a short SDK auth quickstart page before the call.
- HubSpot: I’ve linked RDW-4521 and will push the draft contract template after the handoff.

If that timeline works for you we’ll lock it in.

Best,
